input.message: A tool result can arrive before the next tool call finishes streaming because concurrent tool invocations are often executed asynchronously and independently once their input parameters are fully parsed, rather than waiting for every subsequent call in the same batch to complete its own streaming phase. If one tool has a small payload or a fast backend response, its execution can finish and return output while a sibling tool call, especially one with a larger or more complex argument object, is still being incrementally transmitted token by token from the model. Network latency, payload size, and processing time all vary independently between calls, so completion ordering is decoupled from the order calls were initiated in, meaning results surface asynchronously as each underlying operation actually resolves rather than in strict sequential lockstep with streaming.
